_note: Run MECHANICS -- how a batch executes, independent of which league or decks. Pass alongside a league-identity config (--run-config this, --league-config that); league_main.json's mechanics are pinned equal to these by tests/test_run_league.py. checkpoint_opponent_rate is the one field meant to be overridden per-invocation rather than edited here. Fields that are absent are absent on purpose: games_per_iteration below overrides it, but with no override run_league derives max(1, n_workers) (one game per worker, per its own benchmark comment); the PPO batch-size ramp is hardcoded in rl.train.batch_size_for_iteration; and max_batch_size's safety role belongs to whatever escalation loop health-checks between batches (the /train skill, the webapp).
_values_note: The two non-obvious values, both set 2026-08-13 and both still current. games_per_iteration 24 (not n_workers=6): at 6, every ppo_update spent its whole trust region on six games and approx_kl measured 0.044 against target_kl 0.03 -- early stopping on most updates, epochs_run falling 3.8 -> 2.8 over a run. The larger buffer costs wall-clock without adding collection parallelism; that is the deliberate trade. pfsp_power 0.5 (not 2.0): 2.0 was backwards and sent three of four decks into 58-77% of their games in matchups they win under 25% of -- see rl/league.py's own comment for the measurement.
_identity_note: The 4-deck sub-league was the experiment vehicle for the 2026-08 plateau investigation; its checkpoints were deleted in the 2026-08-17 cleanup, so these identity fields describe a league that would be grown fresh. gauntlet_league_name likewise points at a population that no longer exists -- vs_gauntlet is a documented no-op until the named league has a live.pt, so it stays set and silently starts reporting again if that twin is ever regrown. Whether the gauntlet mechanism survives at all is an open decision (WORK_CHECKLIST.md item 1, C).
